label: bluegecko-3v1-comet-catcher-10
people: [gecko]thebluegecko, lobby skill 34.34 in the header (OS 48 in the ranked duel list per docs/briefs/lessons.md), the opponent, alone in the west; the header lists him as Armada but every unit of his seen was Cortex. The user hosted and watched from the host's seat (computer_whisperer). No spectator spoke.
our_side: Three seats in the east strip under one player: t1 G1 Cortex (seat 0, record-0), t2 H8 Armada (seat 1), t3 G4 Cortex (seat 2). The player was claude-opus-5-5 at effort medium (Claude Code 2.1.283), with no commander role. Each seat's hands were Jev jev-1.13.0 (the banner says jev-latest), in the one-pass era before the hands rebuild. Realtime, in the user's lobby.
summary: Our three seats led on every count we could see from 4:00 to 12:00: 2.2k to 17.3k of army against at most 900 of his in sight, and 34 extractors at 7:00. The lobby's start boxes were not honoured, so the rovers and the picture looked for him in the top rows (which hold our own G1 seat), the player read the empty north as a base in the north-west (B1-C2, marked 5:24), and no unit of ours ever entered A4-C8, where his raids came from. He built turret outposts in the middle (E3/E4 from 6:01, D5 11:25, E6 16:06), raided our south-west-facing spots with Incisor swarms (8:05-11:27), and beat our first push into the west at B3 (12:26-13:36) with Pounders and stun drones. We answered with Lashers: 59 Lashers and 2 Brutes from 13:00 to 18:00, with the army held at D2. As he said himself, that made his tier 2 safe: Tigers from 17:46 and Tzars from 18:22 killed the Lasher mass at D3/E4 (18:43-20:01) and swept G1, G4 and H8 by 26:42. Our own tier-2 plant took 4:03 with about one constructor's build power, because the player's assist steps were dropped.

The first extractor of ours fell at 3:19 (t2 G6). He made his forward line of armed extractors and turrets on the centre column: an Exploiter, a light turret and a radar at E3 at 6:01-6:16, a Twin Guard there at 6:25, E4 at 6:56-7:54, a C1 nest at 7:39-7:40. Later came D5 (a Twin Guard at 11:25), E6 (16:06) and D1 (16:38), and extractors in our south-west (our builders were refused at D6-D8 at 14:26). Incisor swarms of 5-11 came from the south-west through C6 and D5 at 8:03-8:54 and again at 10:50-11:27. Pounders were his defensive body from 5:24 (12 seen before 12:00), with Shuriken stun drones from 12:32 (77 seen in all); 6 Pounders and 3 Brutes held B3 against two of our groups at 12:26. Tier 2 came when our Lashers did, by his own words: a Tiger at 17:46 (D5), a Tzar at 18:22 (E4), an advanced constructor at 22:07, mohos and Scorpions at 22:15-23:27. He swept G1 (23:02-24:42), G4 (24:04-24:50) and H8 (25:57-26:42) with Tzars, Tigers, Rascal swarms (126 seen over the game) and drones. His base, factories and commander were never in our sight.

user_comments.text: Top should stop building other units while doing t2 transition

bears_on.note: This game is the lesson's source. 59 Lashers and 2 Brutes were made from 13:00 to 18:00 with the army held at D2 ('They do NOT go west', 13:16). His first Tiger came at 17:46, and the tier 2 killed 57 Lashers in two fights (18:43-20:01).

'Pounders for defence': 6 Pounders, 3 Brutes and drones held B3 against 21 Brutes and 17 Stouts (12:26-13:36, about 9.5k of ours for 3.5k). Our answer, Lashers to outrange Pounders, loses the sim duel to Pounders (-0.72) and Brutes (-0.65).
We held 5-20x his seen army from 4:00 to 12:00 (12.0k at 10:00 against 560 seen) and never reached his base. The lead was spent in columns E-G and on the empty north row.
The B3 push was two of three groups, already worn (Brutes at 80%). t3's 16 Brutes stayed at F5, and the Stouts lost 7 more at 13:19-13:36 after the Brutes were gone.
The 0:00 packet: 'the rest hold at home'. No soldier of ours went near his real side, A4-C8, all game, while his Rascals were at our G5 by 2:41.

Build power, not metal, bound the top seat's tier 2 after 17:31: about one constructor on the coravp (20-24% a minute) while the store rose to 1,153-1,432. In the user's words, gifted metal is nothing without the build power (3086b7c).

The user's 17:27 comment says the same thing (stop the other lab during the transition), and the player paused plant_8535 at 17:31. Stopping production alone did not speed the plant, since the helpers' assist steps were dropped. The bottleneck was build power.

The relay was said after this game. In the records, the top seat's commander assisted 67 s of the first 4:00 (assist4; pool 50), often from the plant's exit lane (wakes 1:45-4:17). The plant stalled on metal, not build power: stall4 65%, store 2 at 3:00 and 4:00, 11 factory units by 4:00 against the pool's p25 of 16.

We never held or visited anything west of column D below row 2 (A4-C8, D7, D8). His outposts sat at E3/E4/D5/E6 and his extractors in our south-west. Our extractors fell from 34 at 8:00 to 26 at 9:00, peaked at 39 at 18:00, and 72 were lost over the three seats.

His Twin Guard (corhllt) nests at E3/E4 (6:25-7:54), C1 (7:40), D5 (11:25) and E6 (16:06) held the middle. The player kept constructors and groups off them with 'never' lists and cleared them only with the whole ball (8:31, 10:49-11:30).
Exit lanes were blocked by our commanders and builders all game (12 lane wakes). The player's 25:00 note: 'the packet could not move them'.

lens.caveats: No truth file, batch.json or results.jsonl, so his economy, army and base location are unknown and his numbers are floors. minutes.py, analyze_match, floor, raid_ledger, wake_read and hands_window read only record-0 (the top seat); seats 1 and 2 were read through private symlink directories. My first try put those links in the shared scratchpad's seat1/seat2, which belonged to another reader, so the tools read the SD-129 game. Those numbers were thrown away and the other reader's links restored. pro_baseline needs --all-starts, and then it compares one seat of a 3v1 to a duel pool. The date: the batch's unix time reads 2026-09-27 16:54 UTC, but lessons.md, the inbox file and the commit messages date game 10 2026-09-28 (the machine clock ran a day behind the session's dates). chat.jsonl marks the 17:27 line '?'. The record gives it to player 2, the host's seat, without the [WReason] prefix, and the rework design (section 6) makes that the user's comment. The inbox file players-chat-2026-09-28.md gives it to thebluegecko and review.md to a spectator. Where I differ from review.md: (1) The tier-2 plant was not at 0% for three minutes. The 15:40 frame built 7/27/47/71% at 16-19:00 and stood at 19:43. The 0% frame was a second one, started by the player's 18:00 'coravp spot_5' (placed 18:35, dropped 19:15). The cause was build power: dropped assist steps and about one constructor, as the user said (3086b7c). (2) The B3 push was two groups (19-22 Brutes and 17 Stouts at A2 at 12:26), not the top seat's Brutes alone, and it lost about 9.5k with the Stouts. (3) The 0:00 packet did ask scouts for the west strip, so the rovers' box ranking overrode a correct instruction. (4) My three-seat army counts finished units only (12.0k at 10:00 against the review's 12.7k). The rest of the review stands, ranked here by root.

open_questions: Where was his base? It was never seen. His extractors at A4 (seen 12:56) and B3 and the raid routes (Incisors at C6/D5 at 8:03) point to the west middle or south-west (A4-B5), but there is no truth file.

How big were his economy and army at 8:00-12:00, when we held 9-17k against at most 900 seen? Would the 9k ball sent west along rows 3-5 at 8:31 have found and broken his base before his Pounders and drones massed?
